body:
## Summary

Enabling NEXTN (MTP) speculative decoding for `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (GLM-5.3-Flash) with `--tp-size 2` fails while loading the MTP layer's MoE weights. The **target** model loads and serves correctly with the identical command minus the four `--speculative-*` flags; only the draft/MTP worker fails.

The shapes suggest the draft model's `FusedMoE` is constructed **unsharded** while the weight loader supplies the **TP-sharded** slice.

## Environment

- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash-arm64` (the per-model GLM-5.3-Flash image)
- SGLang: `0.0.0.dev1+gd6ab04bdf1`
- Hardware: 2× NVIDIA GB10 (Grace Blackwell, **sm_121**, arm64), 1 GPU per node, TP=2 across 2 nodes over RoCE
- Model: `LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` — weight-only NVFP4 (NVIDIA ModelOpt) of `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`; routed experts NVFP4, everything else BF16. `num_nextn_predict_layers: 1`, and the MTP layer (layer 45, 2617 tensors incl. its own quantized experts) is present in the checkpoint.
- Relevant config: `hidden_size=4096`, `moe_intermediate_size=2048`, `n_routed_experts=288`, `n_shared_experts=1`.

## Reproduction

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code --tp-size 2 --nnodes 2 --node-rank $RANK \
  --dist-init-addr <head>:25100 \
  --attention-backend dsa \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.84 --context-length 65536 --max-running-requests 2 \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2
```

Removing only the four `--speculative-*` flags gives a fully working server (weights load 120/120 on both ranks, KV + mamba caches allocate, generation is correct).

## Traceback

```
  File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 1164, in __init__
  File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 174, in __init__
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/glm5_next.py", line 1705, in load_weights
    weight_loader(
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1016, in weight_loader
    self._weight_loader_physical(
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1046, in _weight_loader_physical
    self._weight_loader_impl(
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1329, in _weight_loader_impl
    self._load_model_weight_or_group_weight_scale(
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 591, in _load_model_weight_or_group_weight_scale
    self._load_w13(
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 703, in _load_w13
    expert_data.copy_(loaded_weight)
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (4096) must match the size of tensor b (2048) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

## Analysis (hypothesis — please sanity-check)

`_load_w13` handles `gate_up_proj`, whose output width is `2 * moe_intermediate_size = 4096` unsharded, or `2048` per rank at TP=2.

- `expert_data` is **4096** wide → the draft model's `FusedMoE` parameter was allocated as if **TP=1**.
- `loaded_weight` is **2048** wide → the loader is supplying the **TP=2** shard.

So the draft/MTP worker and the weight loader appear to disagree about `moe_tp_size` for the NEXTN module. Note this is the *mirror image* of a shape error we hit in the same `_load_w13`/`_load_w2` family for the shared expert, where the param was the sharded one and the checkpoint tensor was full-width — so the sharding assumptions in this path may be worth an audit generally.

We have **not** verified whether this also reproduces with the BF16 upstream checkpoint or at TP=1 on a single node; we only have the 2×GB10 setup. If it is specific to quantized MoE weights in the NEXTN path, that would be useful to know and we are happy to run a requested variant.

## Why it matters

GLM-5.3-Flash is 320B total / 18B active, and on bandwidth-limited hardware decode is bandwidth-bound (we measure ~14.8 tok/s single-stream at TP=2 on 2× GB10, corroborated by SGLang's own `gen throughput` counter). MTP is the main lever that beats a bandwidth wall, and the checkpoint ships the MTP layer specifically for it, so this blocks the single largest available speedup on this class of hardware.

Happy to test patches — we have the cluster available and a full weight load takes ~13 minutes.

comments.body:
The dimension in the traceback points at a different root than TP sharding. The mismatch is at dimension 1, which for `w13_weight` expert data (`[2 * intermediate_per_partition, hidden]`) is the hidden dim, not the TP-sharded output dim. 4096 is `hidden_size` unpacked; 2048 is the same dim NVFP4-packed at two values per byte. At TP=2 the sharded dim 0 agrees by coincidence (allocated `2*2048/2 = 2048` vs loaded shard `4096/2 = 2048`), so the first mismatch to surface is dim 1.

That arithmetic matches #36599: `DeepseekModelNextN.__init__` carries an unconditional override that nulls the quant config whenever it is `modelopt_fp4` (log line: `Overriding DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN quant config for modelopt_fp4 Deepseek model.`), so the draft's FusedMoE is built as unquantized BF16 modules expecting hidden 4096, while your checkpoint's MTP experts are FP4-packed at 2048. The target model is unaffected because the override lives only in the NextN path, which also explains "identical command minus the speculative flags works". State of this at the PR #36507 head, with the fix shape the existing resolver allows: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/36599#issuecomment-5436422199

A one-minute discriminator on the logs you already have, no rerun needed: grep the failing rank for `Overriding DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN quant config`. If it appears right before the draft load, this is #36599 in TP clothing, and the prediction is that it reproduces identically at TP=1 single node, since the dim-1 mismatch is TP-independent. That would take the sharding question out of this particular failure (your mirror-image shared-expert observation may still be worth its own audit). For what a single box can show: on sm_121 the override fires at TP=1 on the current per-model image with dummy weights; the shape crash itself needs real tensors, which do not fit on one 128 GB Spark.

title: [Bug] NEXTN/MTP speculative decoding fails to load MTP MoE weights under TP>1 for Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration (GLM-5.3-Flash)
